content:
I’m starting a new thread for this, since the previous discussion started to mix together quite a few different topics.

I recently added the new AlgebraicFramework to PhyslibAlpha in #1622, and I’m actively developing it further.

At the moment it is still quite math-heavy, but the idea is to build a general and reusable foundation for physical theories formulated in a probabilistic setting. Quantum mechanics is the main application I have in mind, but much of the basic framework is not specifically quantum and applies equally well to things like classical statistical mechanics.

I’d like this thread to be a place to discuss what the right definitions and abstractions should be, both mathematically and from a software/API perspective. Most importantly, I’d like to start gradually porting the mature parts of this framework from PhyslibAlpha into Physlib, so contributions and discussion around that are very welcome.

To give an idea of the basic foundations and how the different layers fit together, I made a short overview:

Probabilistic_Theory.pdf

I should add that I’m not an expert on the mathematical foundations of this subject, so critique is very welcome, in particular if there are better standard definitions, abstractions, or ways of organizing the API.

I’ll also try to join the Physlib Café next Thursday. If people are interested, that would be a good opportunity to discuss some of these questions directly over Zoom / in person and work out what should be upstreamed and how.

I can start to look at this if you share the references (I think you already did but I can't find them now) and the order you want to add this into Physlib. I think keeping the basics very mathematical is a good idea, perhaps upstreaming to Mathlib would be desirable as well.

Sure! Some references that I found useful for understanding the different layers:

  • GPTs / convex theories: the basic idea is to start just with states, measurement outcomes (“effects”), and probabilities. Janotta & Hinrichsen, *Generalized Probability Theories*
  • Ordered / order-unit spaces: a linear formulation of states and effects: states are positive normalized linear maps and effects are elements between (0) and (1). Alfsen & Shultz, *Geometry of State Spaces of Operator Algebras*
  • Jordan / JB algebras: add a symmetric product (a \circ b) between observables. This is enough to talk about squares, positivity, spectral theory, functional calculus, projections, etc. Hanche-Olsen & Størmer, *Jordan Operator Algebras*
  • (C^*)-algebras: add the full associative noncommutative product. Bratteli & Robinson, *Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics*
  • JBW / von Neumann algebras: add the extra completeness needed for things like normal states, spectral measures and infinite systems. Kadison & Ringrose, *Fundamentals of the Theory of Operator Algebras*

In PhyslibAlpha, all of this is currently under the AlgebraicFramework folder. For moving things into Physlib I would start with the most basic layer, called OrderUnit (definitely needs a better name).
Which reference(s) are good for where you want to start?

Daniel Morrison schrieb:

Which reference(s) are good for where you want to start?

I found these references useful in slightly different ways. Janotta & Hinrichsen is a fairly readable and text-heavy introduction to generalized probabilistic theories, while Plávala develops the framework more systematically and contains substantially more of the mathematical details and proofs. I also wrote a short Probabilistic_Theory.pdf, which is my first attempt at organizing the same ideas in a way that keeps the infinite-dimensional setting in mind from the beginning.
@Tom Diem Do you have a candidate file to start the upstream?

Joseph Tooby-Smith schrieb:

Tom Diem Do you have a candidate file to start the upstream?

Yes, I would like to start upstreaming the basics of states and effects which lie in the OrderUnit folder.
Locally I have some 2k loc which I will try to PR (in smaller pieces) this weekend.

I’ve made several PRs: covering states, effects and so on. I’ve called the folder ProbabilisticTheory for now, but I’m very happy to change that as well.

I’d be glad for people to engage with it and leave suggestions, especially on the API, organization, naming or anything that could be made cleaner.

I think "ProbabilisticTheory" seems like a suitable name. We can always change it later if need be.

ccing @David Gross who also might be interested in looking at this?
Yes, thanks for the mention. I was distracted last week, but will comment on the PR soon, hopfully tomorrow.
